responsibility: Defines the compiler’s shared model of Rust type layout and ABI properties, providing the stable data structures, traits, and public APIs that other compiler components use to reason about representation, calling conventions, and machine-level type shape. The crate root (`lib.rs`) establishes and re-exports the fundamental vocabulary for ABI analysis—representation flags, integer and pointer classification, size and alignment, field and variant structure, niche information, layout metadata, and helpers for calling conventions and extern ABI support—so the rest of the compiler can talk about layouts in a uniform way. Its `layout.rs` file supplies the core layout-computation engine that turns those abstractions plus target data layout and `repr` options into concrete `LayoutData` for scalars, aggregates, unions, and enums, determining field placement, ABI form, niches, size/alignment, and reporting layout errors. Together, the crate is the compiler’s central ABI/layout layer: it both defines the canonical concepts for type representation and computes the concrete layouts that code generation and other analyses depend on.
